session.goal: Design a REST API for a work-management platform while requirements evolve across turns around tenancy, backward compatibility, async workflows, webhooks, residency, and naming migration.

content_blocks.text: You are a senior backend architect. Design practical REST APIs, keep backward compatibility explicit, and update prior decisions when requirements change.

I need a v1 REST API for a small work-management product. We have projects, tasks, comments, and assignees. Mobile and web clients both call it. Start simple: CRUD endpoints, token auth, list endpoints, and a status model with todo, doing, done. I also want request and response shapes that are boring enough for external integrators.

For v1, keep the resource graph shallow: `/v1/projects`, `/v1/tasks`, `/v1/comments`, and `/v1/users`. Use bearer tokens, offset pagination for the first pass, ISO-8601 timestamps, and server-generated IDs. Tasks should reference `project_id` and optional `assignee_id`. Comments belong to tasks only. I would expose standard list filters for `project_id`, `status`, and `assignee_id`, but avoid nested write endpoints so the API surface stays stable when you add more task-adjacent objects later.

GET /v1/projects
POST /v1/projects
GET /v1/tasks?project_id=prj_123&status=doing
POST /v1/tasks
PATCH /v1/tasks/{task_id}
GET /v1/tasks/{task_id}/comments
POST /v1/tasks/{task_id}/comments

Requirements changed already. This is now a B2B product, so every object belongs to an organization and some customers want to manage multiple workspaces under the same org. We also need soft delete, auditability, and safe retries from flaky mobile networks. Can you revise the design so creates are idempotent and access control is tenant aware without making every path unreadable?

Do not encode org and workspace in every path unless you want URLs to become the primary authorization mechanism. A cleaner approach is org-scoped tokens plus a required `X-Workspace-Id` header for workspace-bound resources. Keep canonical IDs globally unique, add `deleted_at` for soft delete, and store immutable audit events separately from mutable resource rows. For flaky mobile creates, require `Idempotency-Key` on POST to `/v1/tasks`, `/v1/comments`, and `/v1/projects`; return the original response body for duplicate keys within a retention window. I would also add `GET /v1/audit-events` for admins instead of overloading resource list endpoints with change history.

POST /v1/tasks
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer <org-scoped-token>
  X-Workspace-Id: ws_789
  Idempotency-Key: 8e5c9e42-5d38-4fdb-a3af-1a31eb5b4d8a

{
  "title": "Ship billing fix",
  "project_id": "prj_123",
  "status": "todo"
}

More changes. Attachments are large now, so uploads need to be asynchronous with pre-signed URLs. Search must work across tasks and comments. We already have a legacy `/api/tasks` endpoint used by older clients, and those clients can queue edits offline and sync later. I need a transition plan that keeps old clients alive while new ones move to versioned endpoints.

Split the problem into three tracks. First, keep `/api/tasks` as a compatibility facade that translates to the new service layer, but freeze its schema and document it as deprecated. Second, move the new contract to `/v1/...` and introduce attachment jobs: clients request an upload session, upload directly to object storage, then finalize the attachment against the task. Third, add a sync feed instead of trying to make every list endpoint double as offline transport. Search should be a dedicated endpoint because the result set spans resource types and relevance metadata. That lets you return a normalized envelope with `resource_type`, `resource_id`, `snippet`, and `highlights` while keeping task CRUD predictable.

POST /v1/attachments/upload-sessions
POST /v1/attachments/{upload_session_id}/finalize
GET /v1/search?q=invoice+rollback
POST /v1/sync/pull
POST /v1/sync/push

Compatibility:
  /api/tasks -> translated internally to /v1/tasks semantics where possible
  response headers include Sunset and Link for migration docs

Security and compliance just landed. Some fields are only visible to managers, EU customers need region-pinned storage, and customers want webhooks when status or assignee changes. Webhooks must be signed, retries must be deterministic, rate limits should be per tenant, and bulk updates need partial success reporting because PMs edit many items at once.

At this point the API needs explicit policy surfaces. Keep resource schemas stable, but compute field visibility from role and workspace membership so hidden fields are omitted rather than nulled. Region pinning belongs in tenant provisioning and storage configuration, not in day-to-day request parameters; responses can expose `data_region` for diagnostics. For webhooks, create tenant-managed subscriptions, sign deliveries with an HMAC secret, include a delivery id for replay protection, and treat retries as the same delivery record so duplicate sends remain verifiable. Bulk updates should return `207 Multi-Status` or a 200 envelope with per-item outcomes; I prefer the envelope because many client SDKs handle it more consistently. Rate limit headers should be keyed by tenant and route family, not raw token, otherwise one large customer with multiple integrations will get unpredictable contention.

Final revision. Product wants cursor pagination instead of offset, filtering by `updated_since`, and long-running report exports for enterprise admins. Marketing also wants to rename `task` to `work item` in new docs, but old clients and the old `/api/tasks` route must stay intact for at least a year. Can you converge this into one final API shape with naming and versioning rules that engineering can actually implement?

Final recommendation: keep protocol stability higher than terminology churn. Use `/v1/tasks` as the canonical wire resource for the first major version, but allow docs and SDK models to present `work item` as the user-facing label. Introduce `/v2/work-items` only when you are willing to break names consistently across payloads, search results, webhook event types, and bulk APIs. In v1, standardize on cursor pagination with `limit` and `cursor`, support `updated_since` on list and sync endpoints, and move heavy exports to an async job resource. The compatibility matrix should be explicit: `/api/tasks` remains a frozen facade, `/v1/tasks` is the supported programmable contract, and any renamed terminology lives only in documentation aliases until v2. That gives you one implementable backend model while preserving tenant scoping, idempotent writes, field-level authorization, signed webhooks, region-aware storage, and offline sync semantics introduced earlier in the conversation.

Core v1
GET /v1/tasks?limit=50&cursor=cur_abc&updated_since=2026-04-01T00:00:00Z
POST /v1/tasks
PATCH /v1/tasks/{task_id}
POST /v1/tasks:bulk-update
GET /v1/search?q=priority
POST /v1/report-exports
GET /v1/report-exports/{export_id}
POST /v1/webhook-subscriptions
POST /v1/sync/pull
POST /v1/sync/push

Versioning rules
1. `/api/tasks` stays frozen and deprecated for 12 months.
2. `/v1/tasks` is canonical on the wire even if docs say work items.
3. Reserve `/v2/work-items` for a full naming break with migration tooling.
4. Webhook event names follow wire resources in v1: `task.created`, `task.updated`, `task.status_changed`.
